investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-18T10:44–10:51Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes advertise the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other four nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. Preemption was also unavailable on both node groups. Because the pod never became schedulable, the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner timed out after ~139–146 seconds without collecting any required evidence. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agent pod class in the production-api environment; it is not an eval runner code defect and there is no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident beyond what the eval itself observed.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource capacity is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — all available VM slots are occupied by existing agents or leaked/zombie pods, leaving no room for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely] A quota or resource limit on the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource was reduced (e.g., node pool scaled down, peer-pod provider capacity reduced, or node re-labeling removed eligible nodes), shrinking the schedulable pool below current demand.

[Possible] The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec targets a label that is no longer present on the 4 non-peerpod nodes, meaning those nodes were never eligible and the effective scheduling pool has always been only the 2 peerpod nodes — any saturation of those 2 nodes causes a total scheduling blackout.
[Possible] Leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from prior eval runs or user sessions are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without releasing them, exhausting capacity for new pods.

[Less likely] A change to the Kubernetes node pool configuration (e.g., node drain, maintenance, or label change) reduced the number of nodes advertising kata.peerpods.io/vm from a previously larger count to the current 2.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes had only 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource, both of which reported insufficient capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was written, causing the remote-agent-state expected-output contract to be fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the production-api remote-agent workload has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. With 0 preemption victims available and 4 nodes excluded by node affinity/selector, every new remote-agent pod is left in Pending/Unschedulable state. The eval runner in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent (line 1905) as the first step of the remote-agent-state probe; because that call blocks on pod readiness and the pod never becomes ready, the probe times out without writing any required evidence fields, producing a complete contract gap for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

The withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1903) is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could leave orphaned pods.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-07-18T10:46–10:51Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the 6-node production cluster has no available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity or selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never received a running agent, so zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 production nodes: 2 nodes that match the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource requirement report Insufficient capacity for that resource, and the other 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~144 seconds before the eval timed out. This is a cluster-level infrastructure capacity or configuration problem localized to the remote-agent pod scheduling path in the production-api environment, not a code defect in the eval runner itself. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-infrastructure failure.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: concurrent remote agent pods (from other workloads, prior eval runs, or leaked pods from failed cleanup) have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning only 2 nodes are ever eligible, making the cluster structurally under-provisioned for peak remote-agent demand.
